content.content:
1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison) queries, the reservation/alert listings,
85	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
86	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources`,
87	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations`,
88	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
89	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
90	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
91	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
92	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
93	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
94	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, and the other
95	  read-only branch entry points.
96	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
97	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
98	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
99	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
100	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
101	
102	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
103	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
104	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
105	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
106	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
107	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
108	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
109	is `403`, never `404`.
110	
111	## Event ledger
112	
113	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
114	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
115	
116	### `POST /events`
117	
118	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
119	exactly these five top-level fields:
120	
121	| Field          | Rule                                      |
122	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
123	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
124	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
125	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
126	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
127	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
128	
129	```bash
130	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
131	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
132	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
133	```
134	
135	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
136	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
137	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
138	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
139	  the other fields differ.
140	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
141	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
142	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
143	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
144	
145	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
146	
147	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
148	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
149	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
150	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
151	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
152	
153	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
154	
155	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
156	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
157	organizations' data is never included.
158	
159	Query parameters:
160	
161	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
162	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
163	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
164	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
165	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
166	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
167	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
168	
169	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
170	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
171	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
172	
173	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
174	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
175	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "organizationId": "org-1",
180	  "type": "incident.created",
181	  "windowSize": 60,
182	  "from": null,
183	  "to": null,
184	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
185	}
186	```
187	
188	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
189	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
190	  `windows` is `[]`.
191	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
192	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
193	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
194	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
195	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
196	
197	```bash
198	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
199	```
200	
201	### Region attribution
202	
203	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
204	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
205	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
206	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
207	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
208	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
209	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
210	
211	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
212	
213	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
214	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
215	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
216	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
217	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
218	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
219	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
220	point and a trailing newline.
221	
222	```bash
223	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
224	```
225	
226	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
227	
228	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
229	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
230	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
231	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
232	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
233	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
234	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
235	newline):
236	
237	```json
238	{
239	  "organizationId": "org-1",
240	  "region": "north",
241	  "type": "incident.created",
242	  "windowSize": 60,
243	  "from": null,
244	  "to": null,
245	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
246	}
247	```
248	
249	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
250	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
251	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
252	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
253	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
254	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
255	
256	```bash
257	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
258	```
259	
260	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
261	
262	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
263	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
264	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
265	object containing exactly these fields:
266	
267	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
268	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
269	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
270	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
271	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
272	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
273	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
274	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
275	
276	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
277	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
278	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
279	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
280	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
281	ones for audit reconciliation.
282	
283	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
284	
285	```json
286	{
287	  "organizationId": "org-1",
288	  "type": "incident.created",
289	  "windowSize": 60,
290	  "from": null,
291	  "to": null,
292	  "peakStart": 60,
293	  "peakCount": 2,
294	  "action": "observe"
295	}
296	```
297	
298	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
299	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
300	  regardless of event submission order.
301	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
302	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
303	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
304	  `"observe"`.
305	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
306	  other organizations' data is never included.
307	
308	```bash
309	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
310	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
311	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
312	```
313	
314	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
315	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
316	  produced.
317	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
318	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
319	
320	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
321	
322	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
323	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
324	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
325	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
326	exactly these fields:
327	
328	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
329	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
330	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
331	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
332	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
333	
334	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
335	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
336	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
337	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
338	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
339	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
340	
341	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
342	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
343	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
344	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
345	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
346	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
347	demands.
348	
349	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
350	
351	```json
352	{
353	  "organizationId": "org-1",
354	  "assignments": [
355	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
356	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
357	  ],
358	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
359	  "totalUnits": 6
360	}
361	```
362	
363	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
364	  processing order.
365	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
366	  `demandId`.
367	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
368	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
369	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
370	
371	```bash
372	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
373	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
374	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
375	```
376	
377	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
378	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
379	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
380	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
381	
382	## Reservation inventory
383	
384	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
385	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
386	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
387	is never rewritten afterwards.
388	
389	### `POST /reservations`
390	
391	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
392	with exactly these five top-level fields:
393	
394	| Field           | Rule                                      |
395	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
396	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
397	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
398	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
399	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
400	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
401	
402	```bash
403	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
404	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
405	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
406	```
407	
408	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
409	and a trailing newline:
410	
411	```json
412	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
413	```
414	
415	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
416	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
417	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
418	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
419	
420	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
421	  resource also establishes its capacity.
422	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
423	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
424	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
425	  exists but the other fields differ.
426	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
427	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
428	  capacity is never rewritten.
429	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
430	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
431	  unchanged.
432	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
433	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
434	  is produced.
435	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
436	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
437	
438	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
439	
440	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
441	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
442	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
443	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
444	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
445	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
446	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
447	`422`.

449	## Alert suppression and escalation
450	
451	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
452	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
453	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
454	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
455	paths are added.
456	
457	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
458	
459	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
460	containing exactly these fields:
461	
462	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
463	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
464	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
465	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
466	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
467	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
468	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
469	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
470	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
471	
472	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
473	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
474	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
475	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
476	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
477	
478	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
479	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
480	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
481	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
482	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
483	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
484	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
485	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
486	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
487	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
488	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
489	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
490	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
491	    organization/type always creates an alert.
492	
493	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
494	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
495	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
496	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
497	trailing newline):
498	
499	```json
500	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
501	```
502	
503	```bash
504	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
505	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
506	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
507	```
508	
509	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
510	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
511	  written.
512	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
513	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
514	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
515	
516	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
517	
518	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
519	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
520	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
521	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
522	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
523	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
524	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
525	
526	## Snapshots and branches
527	
528	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
529	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
530	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
531	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
532	the main service or with other branches.
533	
534	### Organization boundaries
535	
536	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
537	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
538	scoped to that boundary:
539	
540	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
541	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
542	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
543	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
544	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
545	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
546	  organization's data never changes them.
547	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
548	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
549	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
550	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
551	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
552	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
553	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
554	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
555	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
556	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
557	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
558	  namespaced per organization.
559	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
560	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
561	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
562	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
563	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
564	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
565	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
566	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
567	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
568	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
569	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
570	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
571	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
572	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
573	
574	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
575	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
576	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
577	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
578	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.
579	
580	### `POST /snapshots`
581	
582	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
583	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
584	
585	| Field        | Rule                     |
586	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
587	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
588	
589	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
590	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
591	JSON:
592	
593	```json
594	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
595	```
596	
597	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
598	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
599	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
600	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
601	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
602	  content is never replaced or mutated.
603	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
604	  organization; no snapshot is stored.
605	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
606	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
607	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, a missing or extra field,
608	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.
609	- Any failed request leaves both the main state and existing snapshots
610	  unchanged.
611	
612	### `GET /snapshots`
613	
614	Returns `200` with `{"snapshots": [...]}`, listing **only the caller
615	organization's** snapshots; other organizations' snapshots are never visible.
616	Each entry has the same shape as a creation response, and entries are sorted
617	by `snapshotId` in Unicode code-point order. With no snapshots the collection
618	is an empty array.
619	
620	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources?organizationId=...`
621	
622	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured resource balances for the
623	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
624	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
625	contract. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the snapshot, in any branch,
626	or in the main service is read for mutation or written: the main-service
627	event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert state are untouched, failed
628	requests leave no trace, and identical requests return byte-for-byte
629	identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. The
630	`organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
631	
632	The `200` response echoes the organization and snapshot identifiers and
633	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the snapshot,
634	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
635	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first captured reservation naming
636	the resource), `occupied` (the sum of every captured reservation the
637	organization holds against the resource — multiple reservations all count),
638	and `remaining` (`capacity - occupied`). Reservations of other
639	organizations never contribute (they are never captured), and a snapshot
640	with no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
641	share the comparison's contract, comparing a snapshot with itself via
642	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources` reports every listed row as `equal`,
643	item by item.
644	
645	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
646	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
647	
648	```json
649	{"organizationId":"org-1","resources":[{"capacity":10,"occupied":3,"remaining":7,"resourceId":"res-a"},{"capacity":4,"occupied":1,"remaining":3,"resourceId":"res-b"}],"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
650	```
651	
652	```bash
653	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/resources?organizationId=org-1' \
654	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
655	```
656	
657	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
658	query shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
659	
660	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
661	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
662	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
663	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
664	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
665	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot
666	  belongs to another organization.
667	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
668	  has never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a snapshot.
669	
670	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
671	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
672	
673	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations?organizationId=...`
674	
675	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured reservations for the
676	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
677	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`, computed from the exact same
678	captured-reservation contract. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the
679	snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or
680	written: the main-service event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert
681	state are untouched, failed requests leave no trace, and identical
682	requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
683	credentials may call it. The `organizationId` query parameter must appear
684	exactly once and be non-empty.
685	
686	The `200` response echoes the organization and snapshot identifiers and
687	carries one row per reservation captured in the snapshot, sorted by
688	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row
689	reports exactly the five reservation fields the reservation comparison
690	aligns on: `organizationId`, `reservationId`, `resourceId`, `quantity`,
691	and `capacity`. Reservations of other organizations never contribute
692	(they are never captured), and a snapshot with no reservations returns an
693	empty `reservations` array. Because the rows share the comparison's
694	contract, comparing a snapshot with itself via
695	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations` lists every reservation in `same`

698	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
699	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
700	
701	```json
702	{"organizationId":"org-1","reservations":[{"capacity":10,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"res-a"}],"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
703	```

705	```bash
706	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/reservations?organizationId=org-1' \
707	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
708	```
709	
710	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
711	query shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
712	
713	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
714	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
715	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
716	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
717	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
718	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot
719	  belongs to another organization.
720	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
721	  has never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a snapshot.
722	
723	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
724	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.

726	### `POST /branches`
727	
728	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
729	must be a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
730	
731	| Field        | Rule                     |
732	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
733	| `branchId`   | non-empty string         |
734	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
735	
736	The new branch receives independent copies of the snapshot's events,
737	resource capacities, and reservation balances (which hold only the snapshot
738	owner organization's data).
739	
740	- `201 Created` — the branch summary is returned:
741	
742	```json
743	{"branchId":"br-1","events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
744	```
745	
746	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the named snapshot exists but
747	  belongs to another organization (ownership is checked before the branch
748	  name), or the credential is read-only. No branch is created and no snapshot
749	  content is returned.
750	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — no snapshot with that
751	  name has ever existed; no branch is created.
752	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "branch_conflict"}`) — the snapshot is owned by
753	  the caller but a branch with that `branchId` already exists anywhere in the
754	  service. The existing branch is unaffected.
755	- `415`, `400`, and `422` follow the same rules as other JSON write
756	  endpoints; `422` (`validation_error`) covers missing, extra, blank, or
757	  non-string fields.
758	
759	### `GET /branches/{branchId}`
760	
761	Returns `200` with the branch summary (see above) when the branch belongs to
762	the caller's organization. A branch owned by another organization returns
763	`403` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and no content. Only a branch name that
764	has never existed returns `404` with `{"error": "branch_not_found"}`.
765	
766	### Branch-prefixed entry points
767	
768	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
769	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
770	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
771	
772	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
773	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
774	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | list the branch's events                  |
775	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events/aggregate`   | aggregate the branch's events             |
776	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | commit an event into the branch only      |
777	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/decisions/evaluate` | evaluate against the branch's events only |
778	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | list the branch's reservations            |
779	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/resources`          | list the branch's resource balances       |
780	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | reserve against branch balances only      |
781	
782	- Branch event commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, identical-replay (`200`),
783	  and `event_id_conflict` (`409`); writes stay in the branch. Name and
784	  capacity comparisons run only against the owning organization's records
785	  that were forked into the branch, so another organization's event
786	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never trigger a
787	  conflict and never affect a branch balance.
788	- Branch reservation commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, and the replay and
789	  capacity rules: identical replays return `200` without double counting,
790	  while `reservation_conflict`, `capacity_conflict`, and
791	  `capacity_exceeded` still return `409`; a failed commit never changes the
792	  branch inventory.
793	- Branch list and aggregate queries apply the same parameter rules as the
794	  main endpoints; missing, duplicated, or empty parameters return `422` with
795	  `validation_error`.
796	- Branch evaluation is read-only over branch events, and branch aggregates
797	  never count main-service events; repeated identical requests return
798	  identical results.
799	- No branch operation creates or rolls back main-service state, and branches
800	  never observe each other's writes. Unknown sub-paths under a known branch
801	  return the standard JSON `404`; sub-paths under an unknown branch return
802	  `branch_not_found`.
803	- The region queries (`/events/region` and `/events/region/aggregate`) are
804	  main-only; no branch-prefixed region paths are added.
805	- `/decisions/allocate` remains a main-only, stateless endpoint.
806	
807	### `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources?organizationId=...`
808	
809	A read-only listing of one branch's current resource balances for the
810	caller's organization — the single-branch counterpart of
811	`POST /branches/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
812	contract. Nothing in the branch, in any other branch, or in the main
813	service is read for mutation or written, alert state is untouched, and
814	identical requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and
815	`write` credentials may call it. The `organizationId` query parameter
816	must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
817	
818	The `200` response echoes the organization and branch identifiers and
819	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the branch,
820	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
821	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first reservation naming the
822	resource in the branch), `occupied` (the sum of every reservation the
823	organization holds against the resource in that branch — multiple
824	reservations all count), and `remaining` (`capacity - occupied`).
825	Reservations of other organizations never contribute, and a branch with
826	no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
827	share the comparison's contract, comparing a branch with itself via
828	`POST /branches/compare/resources` reports every listed row as `equal`.
829	
830	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
831	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
832	
833	```json
834	{"branchId":"br-1","organizationId":"org-1","resources":[{"capacity":10,"occupied":3,"remaining":7,"resourceId":"res-a"},{"capacity":4,"occupied":1,"remaining":3,"resourceId":"res-b"}]}
835	```
836	
837	```bash
838	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/br-1/resources?organizationId=org-1' \
839	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
840	```
841	
842	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
843	query shape, then the organization, and only then the branch name.
844	
845	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
846	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
847	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
848	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
849	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
850	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named branch belongs
851	  to another organization.
852	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — the branch name has
853	  never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a branch.
854	
855	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
856	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
857	
858	### `POST /branches/compare`
859	
860	A read-only comparison of two existing branches' window counts and peak
861	decisions. Each side recomputes its window counts and peak from that
862	branch's own events only; nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or
863	in the main service is read for mutation or written, and identical
864	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
865	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
866	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
867	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
868	
869	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
870	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
871	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
872	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
873	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
874	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
875	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
876	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
877	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
878	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
879	
880	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
881	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
882	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
883	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
884	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
885	
886	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
887	  hit by matching events on either side, aligned row-by-row by `start`
888	  ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's count as
889	  `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
890	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
891	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
892	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
893	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
894	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
895	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
896	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
897	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
898	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
899	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
900	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
901	
902	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
903	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
904	newline:
905	
906	```json
907	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"br-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"br-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
908	```
909

1349	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose `organizationId`, `resourceId`,
1350	  `quantity`, and `capacity` all match.
1351	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides that disagree in at least one of those
1352	  four fields. Each entry is `{"reservationId", "fields"}`, where `fields`
1353	  names the mismatched fields, drawn only from `organizationId`,
1354	  `resourceId`, `quantity`, and `capacity`; no other content participates
1355	  in the comparison.
1356	
1357	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
1358	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
1359	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
1360	neither snapshot holds any reservation for the organization, all four
1361	groups are empty arrays and all four counts are `0`.
1362	
1363	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1364	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1365	
1366	```json
1367	{"diff":[{"fields":["capacity","quantity"],"reservationId":"res-2"}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["res-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["res-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["res-3"],"sameCount":1}
1368	```
1369	
1370	```bash
1371	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/compare/reservations \
1372	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1373	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1374	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"snap-a","right":"snap-b"}'
1375	```
1376	
1377	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1378	  registered.
1379	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1380	  different organization, or one of the named snapshots belongs to another
1381	  organization. The organization decision happens before snapshot names are
1382	  inspected, and snapshots are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1383	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1384	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1385	  `right` has never existed as a snapshot. Both participating snapshots
1386	  must already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1387	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1388	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1389	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1390	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1391	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1392	
1393	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1394	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1395	
1396	### `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`
1397	
1398	A read-only, resource-capacity comparison of two existing snapshots. Where
1399	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations` aligns captured reservations by
1400	`reservationId`, this entry point aligns the resources the two snapshots
1401	captured at their own creation times, by `resourceId`, and compares the two
1402	sides' three resource balances — `capacity`, `occupied`, and `remaining`.
1403	Nothing in either snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read
1404	for mutation or written — snapshots are immutable, alert state is untouched,
1405	and identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read`
1406	and `write` credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type:
1407	application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the request's
1408	`organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object containing exactly these
1409	fields:
1410	
1411	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1412	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1413	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both snapshots must belong to it |
1414	| `left`           | required, non-empty snapshot name (the left-hand side)      |
1415	| `right`          | required, non-empty snapshot name (the right-hand side)     |
1416	
1417	Using the same snapshot name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1418	are then the same capture and every row's `equal` marker is true.
1419	
1420	Resources are aligned by `resourceId`. The `resources` array carries one row
1421	per resource in the union of the two sides, sorted by `resourceId` in
1422	Unicode code-point order. Each row is
1423	`{"resourceId", "left", "right", "equal"}`, where `left` and `right` each
1424	hold the three balances `capacity`, `occupied`, and `remaining`. A resource
1425	missing on one side is treated as absent and that side's three balances are
1426	all `0`. `equal` is true exactly when the two sides' three balances all
1427	agree, and false when any one of them differs.
1428	
1429	In addition to the rows, four grouping arrays partition the resources:
1430	
1431	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left snapshot.
1432	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right snapshot.
1433	- `same` — identifiers present on both sides whose `capacity`, `occupied`,
1434	  and `remaining` all match.
1435	- `diff` — identifiers present on both sides that disagree in at least one
1436	  of those three balances. Each entry is `{"resourceId", "fields"}`, where
1437	  `fields` names the mismatched balances, drawn only from `capacity`,
1438	  `occupied`, and `remaining`.
1439	
1440	A resource present on only one side is never placed in `same` or `diff`; it
1441	appears only in `leftOnly`/`rightOnly` (its row still carries a zeroed
1442	opposite side). Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point
1443	order. Each group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group
1444	plus `Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`).
1445	When neither snapshot holds any resource, the `resources` array and all four
1446	groups are empty and all four counts are `0`.
1447	
1448	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1449	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
1450	newline:
1451	
1452	```json
1453	{"diff":[{"fields":["occupied","remaining"],"resourceId":"res-2"}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["res-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"resources":[{"equal":false,"left":{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"remaining":3},"resourceId":"res-1","right":{"capacity":0,"occupied":0,"remaining":0}},{"equal":false,"left":{"capacity":10,"occupied":4,"remaining":6},"resourceId":"res-2","right":{"capacity":10,"occupied":7,"remaining":3}},{"equal":true,"left":{"capacity":8,"occupied":2,"remaining":6},"resourceId":"res-3","right":{"capacity":8,"occupied":2,"remaining":6}}],"rightOnly":[],"rightOnlyCount":0,"same":["res-3"],"sameCount":1}
1454	```
1455	
1456	```bash
1457	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/compare/resources \
1458	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1459	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1460	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"snap-a","right":"snap-b"}'
1461	```
1462	
1463	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1464	  registered.
1465	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1466	  different organization, or one of the named snapshots belongs to another
1467	  organization. The organization decision happens before snapshot names are
1468	  inspected, and snapshots are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1469	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1470	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1471	  `right` has never existed as a snapshot. Both participating snapshots
1472	  must already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1473	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1474	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1475	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1476	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1477	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1478	
1479	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1480	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
